heading: server/application.json, field by field
body: This file is the configuration of Yon, and the file itself is the yon namespace. Its members are yon.* paths with no root key, so server.port is yon.server.port. Tachyon reads server, datasource, redis, topics and outgoing. server takes only host, port, hosts, proxies, environment and maxbody; with any other member of server the server does not start, and its message names the members it accepts. (server/packages/ is a folder for the native Go packages of Go Yon code, not a key; see Native Go packages.) server.hosts lists the extra names that a loopback server answers (`TY1366`), server.proxies lists the reverse proxies whose forwarding headers count (see The client address and forwarding headers), server.environment lists the variables of `ty`'s environment that handler processes may see, as names or prefix patterns such as `HD_*` (see Environment variables for handlers), topics.directory names the folder of the topic logs (data/topics unless set), and outgoing.hosts lists the hosts that Yon code may send requests to, and every other host is refused when Tachyon builds and when it runs (`TY1326`). Every other member belongs to the application, which reads it with Setting or Settings. A profile (a set of settings for one environment) is a file server/application-<profile>.json that YON_PROFILE selects. It has the same shape and merges over the base file, so its values win over the base values. Secrets never go in this file. A password is a YON_ name in the .env file at the project root. The file refuses names that look like secrets and URLs that contain credentials. Tachyon also reads the migration settings `cohesion.check`, `duplication.check`, `dependencies.check`, `names.check`, `signatures.check`, `constants.check`, `visibility.check`, `types.check` (off until you set it to `true`) and `tests.check` (the test-case rule `TY1339`, see Test units): `false` turns that build rule off for Yon code while you migrate. `simplify.suggest` set to `false` hides the simpler-form suggestions for Yon code (see Simpler forms). `implicitmembers.suggest` set to `true` shows the receiver suggestions for Yon code too (off by default). `names.words` lists words of your domain that Yon names may use.
